target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Meet v2 + Drive files.export request deadlines
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google Meet v2, Drive transcript export, and OAuth token requests could wait indefinitely when Google accepted a connection but never returned response headers.

## Why This Change Was Made

- centralize all Meet v2 transport setup in one private `requestGoogleMeetApi` helper
- enforce an owner-controlled 30-second deadline at the Meet v2, Drive export, and OAuth request boundaries
- keep caller APIs unchanged; callers cannot disable or override the safety policy
- cover the only remaining Google request sibling after the Calendar deadline landed in #102157

This replaces the original optional-timeout plumbing and 222-line loopback harness with one canonical production path and a 69-line fake-timer regression suite.

## User Impact

Stalled Google API requests now fail with the shared `TimeoutError` after 30 seconds instead of hanging Google Meet lookup, artifact export, room creation, conference shutdown, or OAuth refresh flows indefinitely.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/request-timeouts.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 3/3 passed on the rebased head
- brokered Linux Crabbox `run_541d202caf5f` — 3/3 timeout regressions passed on Node 24
- brokered Linux Crabbox `run_894c5eb27572` — all 17 Google Meet test files / 204 tests passed
- brokered Linux Crabbox `run_b280a8819214` — `pnpm check:changed` passed, including extension and test typechecks, lint, database-first guard, sidecar guard, and import-cycle scan
- fresh Codex autoreview — no actionable findings, correctness confidence 0.98
- live endpoint probes against the documented Meet v2 spaces/conferenceRecords routes, Drive `files.export`, and Google OAuth token route all reached Google and returned the expected unauthenticated 401 response

Blacksmith Testbox warmup was unavailable because its workflow fetch returned HTTP 429, so the same proof ran on a brokered public-network AWS Crabbox. No credentials were used in the live endpoint probes.
